issue.title: test_owner_child_shares_wrapper_group_and_group_kill_leaves_no_survivors sees child alive after waiting for killed wrapper
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1ou.2.1.2 note 3 while verifying ToolRun SQLite contention. In the frozen after stress run, loaded iteration 11 failed tests/tool/test_wrapper_fidelity.py::test_owner_child_shares_wrapper_group_and_group_kill_leaves_no_survivors at line 231, assert not _alive(child_pid), immediately after killpg(SIGKILL) and wrapper.wait. Both process-group assertions had succeeded. No SQLite exception occurred. Rate: 1/20 loaded (-n 8 plus four SHA256 CPU loops and an 8 MiB fsync writer), 0/10 serial. The same unchanged integrated tree then passed the complete file 8/8 and this node 3/3 in controlled runs. The final corrected core run also passed 10/10 serial and 20/20 loaded; this does not erase the earlier flake.

Likely an exit-order assertion race: waiting for the wrapper does not establish that its child has exited. This is an inference, not yet a demonstrated root cause; do not assume permanent child survival or weaken the assertion. Diagnose using deterministic process exit observation and distinguish zombie/reaping state from a surviving process. Keep the existing baseline active until proved fixed.

Use the frozen run.py and logs in file:explicit:b13e06f116130351ef4438d2, especially after/loaded-11; the audited final report file:explicit:b0d1fd4be5d7f8c6c632927d preserves exact rates. No process-group production or test code was changed by the contention epic. Closed sase-19c was superseded into sase-18t because its captured failures were database-is-locked; that closure does not cover this assertion signature. No matching open task or causally owning active epic was found. Size large because the cause remains unproven and needs a reproduction/design before implementation.

issue.creation_reason: Landing triage found a distinct non-SQLite assertion flake reported by sase-1ou.2.1.2; existing database-lock tasks do not cover its signature.

payload.description: Historical wrapper tests overlap, but closed task captured SQLite busy rather than child-alive assertion
Keep group-kill assertion flake separate from the ToolRun SQLite contention mechanism
Confirm the distinct follow-up from phase 2 is ready and retains its evidence

payload.entry: sase-1ou landing (2026-10-28): the flake baseline now lists both tests/tool/test_wrapper_fidelity.py group-kill nodes under # sase-1p2, moved from the closing sase-18t. The inline-caller node test_inline_caller_group_sigkill_leaves_no_survivors is the same file's sibling group-kill assertion. It has 5 gate-countable failures, last 2026-10-11, and never the SQLite busy signature.
